To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a “triple spike isotope dilution” approach has been employed for in vitro gastrointestinal digestion studies of butyltin (BT) species, (2) the degradation and solublisation of BT species during in vitro digestion has been monitored, (3) the degradation of DBT to MBT is the most serious degradation observed, (4) the solubilised butyltin content after complete gastrointestinal digestion of a mussel tissue was 61% of that present in
the “triple spike isotope dilution” approach can be used to study the degradation and solulibisation of butyl tin species during in vitro gastrointestinal digestions.

the degradation factors of MBT, DBT, and TBT calculated in this work are in agreement with those reported by previous works, whereas a high solubilisation degree of butyltin was observed after complete simulated digestion.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of a “triple spike approach” in combination with an in vitro gastrointestinal digestion procedure in order to study the transformation and solubilising reactions of butyltin in a solid biological matrix.
the use of “triple spike isotope dilution” for the determination of butyltin concentrations and interconversion reactions in biological matrices.
the development of a method for the study of the degradation and solublisation of butyltins during in vitro gastrointestinal processes using “triple-spike” isotope dilutions GC-ICPMS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gastrointestinal digestion of butyltin-containing matrices is not a simple and straightforward procedure, as it is usually thought to be, since it is a complex process involving several interconversion and degradation reactions as well as a significant fraction of the total butyltin present in a sample being solubilised.
TBT is not only highly stable in the digestive tract, but it is also highly soluble and thus highly bioavailable.
the gastrointestinal tract is a major pathway for the release of butyltin into the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “triple spike isotope dilution” approach is a very useful and reliable technique to study the transformation and solubilization of butyltin during simulated gastrointestinal digestion.
a “triple spike isotope dilution” approach is a useful and reliable tool for the analysis of the degradation and solulbilisation of butyltins during in vitro digestion procedures.
a triple spike approach can be successfully applied for the study of the transformation reactions and the solubilization of butyltin during simulated human digestion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of isotopic dilution analysis, combined with the in vitro digestion procedure, is an excellent approach for the study of the degradation and solublisation of butyltins during gastrointestinal digestion.
, in order to avoid overestimation of the butyl tin degradation factors, the use of a “triple spike approach” is recommended.
in vitro gastrointestinal digestion is a useful technique to evaluate the bioavailability and the transformation reactions of butyltin in the digestive system.
